newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end mixed after range trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end mixed after range trade.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals ended mixed on Monday in lacklustre and rangebound trade, as the market received few clues from the currency market, traders said.
TOCOM's most-active June 1997 contract settled three yen lower at 1,341 yen. Other contracts ranged from two yen per gram lower to one yen firmer.
The platinum spot August contract was lifted by technically driven short-covering ahead of the spot expiry on Tuesday. It rose nine yen to 1,410 yen. Benchmark June ended two yen lower at 1,379 yen.
Open interest of TOCOM gold futures fell to 427,420 lots as of Friday, down from 437,052 lots on August 15.
Silver futures ranged from 2.2 yen per 10 grams lower to 0.3 yen firmer. Benchmark June ended 0.1 yen up at 183.8 yen.

Palladium futures ranged from four yen per gram lower to two firmer, with benchmark June ending two yen firmer at 439 yen. Open interest of palladium futures rose to 23,881 lots as of last Friday, up from 18,669 lots on August 15.
"Physical buying after spot palladium fell to 2-1/2 year lows in mid August, helped lift open interest," another trader said. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk (81-3 3432 7431)
